claim.summary: DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions() must force the settings manager into the untrusted project state (and reload settings in that state) before resolving packages and loading extensions, so project-local extensions can never execute during the trust-bootstrap pass, even when the previous trust state was trusted; user/global and temporary CLI extensions must still load.

citations.note: Bootstrap pass: previously called this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(true), leaving (or escalating to) the trusted state, so project settings/packages/extensions leaked into the pre-trust extension set. Now forces setProjectTrusted(false) before reload() and the extension resolution pass.

Calls loadProjectTrustExtensions() before invoking options.resolveProjectTrust, so the bootstrap extension set is what the user's trust decision is based on; project extensions are only added by the later loadFinalExtensionSet pass once trust is granted.

Semantics relied on: setting the same trust value is a no-op, false drops project settings from the effective settings (and blocks project writes); this is why forcing untrusted must happen explicitly rather than assuming a prior false state.
reload() re-reads project settings using the current projectTrusted flag, so forcing untrusted must occur before reload for project settings to be excluded.

citations.symbol: should load user extensions before trust and reuse them after trust resolves
citations.note: Existing intent test: the pre-trust extension set contains only the user/global extension, and the project extension appears only after trust resolves.

validation.notes: Standalone Node 24 script (verified on v24.14.0) with no installed dependencies and no network. It loads the real production module packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts via .prale-eval/subject.mjs loadModule() and supplies its own boundary fakes for chalk, path/paths helpers, the event bus, the extension loader, footer-data-provider, package-manager, prompt-templates, skills, source-info and timings. FakePackageManager models real behavior by deriving package extension lists from the fake SettingsManager's effective settings, so project extensions only surface while the project is trusted. Scenario 1 (previous state trusted, calls loadProjectTrustExtensions directly): asserts the bootstrap loads only the CLI and user/global extensions, never the project extension, that setProjectTrusted(false) is issued before the first settings reload, that the first reload happens with trusted=false, and that every package-resolution pass in the bootstrap observes an untrusted project. Scenario 2 (full reload with a resolveProjectTrust hook from a previously trusted state): asserts the callback sees an untrusted settings manager and an extension set of exactly [cli, global], then that the project extension is loaded by the final pass once trust is granted, with user/global and CLI extensions still present. Scenario 3 (previous state untrusted) asserts the bootstrap never escalates trust. Result: exits 0 on the repaired code. Replaying the same script against the original fault (setProjectTrusted(true)) exits 1 with 'AssertionError: trust bootstrap must load only CLI and user/global extensions, got [global-ext.ts, cli-ext.ts, project-ext.ts]'. Limitation recorded: the repository's own vitest suite (packages/coding-agent/test/resource-loader.test.ts, including 'should load user extensions before trust and reuse them after trust resolves') could not be run because node_modules is not installed in this sandbox and installing dependencies is out of scope; the standalone regression substitutes for it by exercising the same production code path with faked collaborators.
